entries.title: Called Claude Control everywhere
notes: Messages, settings and screens now say "Claude Control" where they used to say "the board".

entries.title: Paste works in the terminal and Files
notes: Paste from the clipboard now works in the terminal and Files.
The start-up screen no longer flashes inside the terminal.

entries.title: A simpler tray menu
notes: The temporary Remove old web-app installs item is gone.

entries.title: Calmer tray, a friendlier start-up, one toast for many
notes: The tray icons carry a small dot: orange when a session waits on you, a hollow ring when the board cannot be reached; nothing when all is quiet. The tooltip says how many wait (and for how long, the oldest) and how many are working.

Several sessions needing you at once give one notification listing them, and every session or usage notification has an Open button. Set quiet_hours (start and end, such as 22:00 and 07:00) in settings.json to hold notifications back at night; the tray icon still shows them.

The start-up screen has a new three-dot animation, says it is connecting to your board, counts down to its next try (3 seconds growing to 30), and lists what usually fixes it. A calm loading veil covers the window while the board page loads.
The microphone is allowed for the board's Voice and Ask bar without a prompt each time; camera, location, notifications and clipboard reading are refused rather than asking again and again.
The window's place and size are saved shortly after you move or resize it, not only when you close it.

entries.title: Open Tunnel Control and RBV Control from the tray
notes: The tray menu is tidier: settings, board address and clean-up moved into a Settings submenu; the common actions stay on top.

The tray menu lists Tunnel Control and RBV Control when they are installed on this PC, shows when each is running, and opens it with one click. Apps that only exist on Android (CC Companion) are never offered here.
Sessions waiting on you appear in the tray menu, and clicking one (or its notification) opens that session's page.
The 5-hour tray icon pulses gently while a session is working, and is still when nothing is.
The start-up screen fades in, announces connection problems to screen readers, and respects Windows' reduced-motion setting.

entries.title: Tells the board which apps are running
notes: Claude Control now shows Tunnel Control as Running while it is open on this PC. Its SSH forwards leave nothing on the Dell to see, so this app tells the board instead.
RBV Control shows as running even when its tunnel to the Dell is down, and says so.
The PC is checked every 2 minutes. While an app is open it is reported again every 5 minutes, so after the PC sleeps it stops showing as running within about 12 minutes.

entries.title: Updates from GitHub; tray numbers stay coloured
notes: Updates now come from app-releases on GitHub, so they arrive wherever the PC is, not only on the tailnet.
Each download's size and SHA-256 are checked before it replaces the app, as before.
When GitHub cannot be reached, it updates from the board on the Dell instead.

The tray numbers keep their colour when no Claude session has run for a while, or the board is out of reach; they used to turn grey. The tooltip says how old the figure is, and a limit whose reset time has passed shows 0%.

entries.title: Bigger, crisper tray numbers
notes: The numbers in the tray icons fill their tiles and are sharper at every display scaling.

entries.title: Tray numbers coloured by their value
notes: Both tray tiles use one colour scale: green to 50%, amber around 70% and red from 90%.
The tooltip says which tile is the 5-hour limit and which is the weekly one.

entries.title: Two usage numbers in the tray, and the old web app cleaned up
notes: Two tray icons: your 5-hour and weekly usage, each with its own tooltip and reset time.
Uses the board's own icon, and tells the board which family apps are installed on this PC.
Removes the old Claude Control web-app installs and the old PowerShell tray, and never installs an older version over a newer one.

entries.title: Claude Control for Windows
notes: The board in a window of its own, with your usage in the notification area and Windows notifications when a session needs you.
Installs itself like a normal Windows app, starts with Windows if you want, and updates itself from the board.
Replaces the old PowerShell tray script, which it removes.
